title: Pork, potatoes, and vegetables excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy; tomato‑based sauce

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of lean pork, boiled or roasted potatoes, and a mix of vegetables, deliberately excluding carrots, broccoli, and dark‑green leafy greens. All components are topped with a tomato‑based sauce made from ripe tomatoes, onion, garlic, and spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork is one of the most widely consumed meats worldwide, with production steadily increasing.
Potatoes rank fourth in global food production, providing roughly 20 % of the world’s caloric intake.
Tomato sauce is rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant whose availability improves with cooking.
Excluding carrots, broccoli, and leafy greens is often done due to specific allergies or dietary restrictions.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork supplies all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Tomatoes in the sauce provide a good amount of vitamin C, which aids immune function.

items.title: Potassium and magnesium
items.content: Both potatoes and tomatoes deliver potassium and magnesium, important for heart and muscle health.

items.title: Reduced carbohydrate impact after cooking
items.content: Baking or roasting potatoes breaks down some starch, making the dish more moderate in carbohydrate load.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: The remaining vegetables add dietary fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Certain cuts of pork can be high in saturated fat; choosing lean cuts is recommended.

items.title: Salt in the sauce
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or their derivatives.

items.title: Potential pathogens in pork
items.content: Pork must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C to eliminate salmonella and trichinella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course, paired with boiled rice or whole‑grain pasta. Vegetables can be steamed or lightly sautéed, and the tomato sauce used as a topping or a light marinade.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it remains good for up to 2 months after cooling to room temperature.
